title: Aloo Gobi
subtitle: Indian spiced potato and cauliflower dry curry
excerpt: One of the most satisfying dry vegetable curries: potatoes and cauliflower fried in spiced oil until golden and tender, cooked dry so that the spices cling to every piece rather than pooling in a sauce. Simple, deeply flavoured, and endlessly versatile.

recipe.sourceNotes: Aloo gobi (potato cauliflower) is a dry vegetable curry that is eaten across North India and Pakistan as a daily home dish. It is a sukhi sabzi (dry vegetable preparation) rather than a wet curry, which means there is very little or no water added and the cooking relies on the steam from the vegetables themselves. The dish became briefly famous in Britain through the 1999 film Bend It Like Beckham, in which it appears as a symbol of domestic Indian cooking in the British-Punjabi diaspora. The trick to a good aloo gobi is patience: the vegetables should be cooked over medium heat with occasional stirring rather than constant attention, allowing each piece to develop colour and absorb the spices without becoming mushy.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, heavy frying pan or casserole with a lid.

content.text: Do not add water: this is a dry curry and the vegetables cook in their own moisture. If they stick, lower the heat rather than adding water. The cauliflower should be cut into small florets, about 3 cm, to ensure it cooks in the same time as the potato. Take the time to brown the potato pieces before adding the cauliflower; the browning adds depth and texture.

items.preparation: peeled and cut into 2.5 cm cubes
small to medium; broken into 3 cm florets

content.text: Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Add the turmeric, coriander, cumin, and chilli powder and stir for 30 seconds.

Add the potato cubes and toss to coat in the spiced oil. Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring every 2 to 3 minutes, until the potato pieces are golden on most sides. Add the cauliflower florets and stir to combine.

Season with salt. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring gently every 4 minutes, until both the potato and cauliflower are tender. Remove the lid for the final 3 minutes to drive off any steam and re-crisp the edges. Add the garam masala, scatter with coriander, and serve.
